result.description: Vespa crabro specimen analyzed with Claude Vision.
result.first_aid: Wash sting site with soap/water. Apply ice pack.
result.interesting_facts: Smooth stinger allows multiple defensive stings.

result.threat_explanation: Large social wasp with painful venomous sting. Not typically aggressive away from nest but defends territory vigorously within 3-5 meters.
result.pet_child_explanation: Children and curious pets should maintain at least 5 meters distance. Smooth stinger can deliver multiple stings without detachment.
result.description: Vespa crabro is Europe's largest native eusocial wasp. Queens reach 25-35 mm, workers 18-24 mm. Characterized by rich reddish-brown thorax and head vertex with yellow-striped abdomen.
result.habitat: Deciduous woodlands, mature gardens, tree hollows, and occasionally sheltered roof eaves.
result.first_aid: Wash the sting site thoroughly with soap and warm water. Apply cold ice pack wrapped in cloth for 15-20 minutes. Keep limb elevated. Take oral antihistamine if moderate swelling occurs.
result.when_to_call_emergency: Call emergency services (112/999/911) immediately if shortness of breath, wheezing, throat swelling, dizziness, or widespread hives occur (anaphylaxis signs).

pest_control.treatment_method: Do not attempt to disturb or remove active nests yourself. Contact licensed pest control professionals if nest is adjacent to doorways.
pest_control.natural_solutions: Place decoy wasp nests early in spring to deter queen establishment.
pest_control.prevention: Seal gaps around fascia boards and attic vents before spring queen emergence.

result.interesting_facts: Unlike honey bees, the European hornet possesses a smooth stinger that does not dislodge, allowing repeated defensive stings without dying.

scan_jm_001.notes: Observed near old oak tree at forest edge. Very active during warm afternoon.

result.threat_explanation: Invasive predatory hornet across Europe. Highly aggressive when nest is approached within 5-10 meters. Serious threat to domestic honeybee colonies.
result.pet_child_explanation: Severe venom reaction risk. Keep children and pets away from high tree canopies or hedgerows where secondary nests form.
result.description: Vespa velutina is an invasive hornet species recognized by its distinctly dark brown/black velvety thorax and abdomen with a single orange segment (4th tergite) and bright yellow leg extremities.
result.habitat: Urban parks, orchards, tall tree crowns, and apiary vicinities.
result.first_aid: Immediately move away from sighting area. Disinfect sting area with antiseptic. Apply cold compress and monitor closely for allergic reactions.
result.when_to_call_emergency: Call emergency (112) immediately upon any facial swelling, breathing constriction, rapid heart rate, or after receiving multiple stings.

pest_control.treatment_method: Report immediately to local environmental/agricultural authorities for official nest destruction. Never attempt DIY removal.
pest_control.natural_solutions: Selective baited traps in early spring around apiaries.
pest_control.prevention: Support local beekeeping association surveillance networks.

result.interesting_facts: A single Asian hornet can capture up to 30 honeybees per day by hovering outside hive entrances and ambushing returning foragers.

scan_jm_002.notes: Spotted hovering near backyard beehives. Characteristic yellow leg tips and dark velvet thorax.

result.threat_explanation: Docile beneficial pollinator. Only stings in direct self-defense (e.g. if stepped on or grabbed) or near hive entrance.
result.pet_child_explanation: Low risk unless stepped on barefoot or if a known bee allergy exists. Do not disturb active apiary hives.
result.description: Apis mellifera is the primary domesticated honey bee worldwide. Golden brown to black striped abdomen with fuzzy thorax and pollen baskets (corbiculae) on hind legs.
result.habitat: Flowering meadows, gardens, agricultural orchards, and managed hives.
result.first_aid: Scrape away the barbed stinger immediately with a fingernail or blunt card edge (do not squeeze stinger venom sac). Wash with soap and apply ice.
result.when_to_call_emergency: Call emergency medical services if systemic allergic reaction occurs (hives away from sting site, throat tightness, dizziness).

pest_control.treatment_method: Protected agricultural pollinator. Never use insecticide. If a swarm settles on your property, call a local beekeeper for free live relocation.

result.interesting_facts: Honey bee workers perform an intricate 'waggle dance' inside the hive to communicate the exact direction and distance of floral nectar sources to other bees.

scan_jm_003.notes: Foraging on lavender blossoms in community garden. Very docile behavior.

result.threat_explanation: Caterpillar stage carries up to 63,000 microscopic barbed hairs containing the toxic protein thaumetopoein, causing severe dermatitis, conjunctivitis, and asthma.
result.pet_child_explanation: Extremely hazardous to dogs and children. Hairs remain toxic on forest floors for years and can cause severe tongue necrosis in dogs.
result.description: Thaumetopoea processionea larvae march in nose-to-tail processions. Late instar caterpillars are covered in greyish-white setae and thousands of microscopic toxic release hairs.
result.habitat: Oak trees (Quercus robur, Quercus petraea) in parks, woods, and urban avenues.
result.first_aid: Do not rub affected skin. Use adhesive tape to gently lift remaining hairs from skin. Wash skin and eyes with copious water. Wash contaminated clothes at 60°C.
result.when_to_call_emergency: Seek immediate emergency medical care if breathing distress, severe eye inflammation, or allergic anaphylactoid shock develops.

pest_control.treatment_method: Professional vacuum removal with HEPA filters and full protective hazmat equipment. Bacillus thuringiensis biological spray in early spring.
pest_control.natural_solutions: Install specialized nest boxes for Great Tits and Blue Tits which predate early-instar larvae.
pest_control.prevention: Avoid walking under infested oak trees during late spring and early summer.

result.interesting_facts: The toxic microscopic hairs are barbed like harpoons and can drift on the wind for hundreds of meters from oak branches.

scan_jm_004.notes: Silken nest found at base of oak branch in municipal park. Reported to park rangers.

result.threat_explanation: Completely harmless to humans, children, and pets. Exceptional biological pest control agent for gardens.
result.pet_child_explanation: Entirely safe for children to observe and handle gently. Does not sting or bite.
result.description: Coccinella septempunctata is Europe's most common ladybird beetle. Red elytra with exactly seven black spots (three on each wing case and one spread over the suture).
result.habitat: Agricultural crops, herbaceous borders, shrubs, rose bushes, and meadows rich in aphids.
result.first_aid: No medical treatment needed. If yellowish reflex blood stains fingers, simply wash with regular soap and water.

pest_control.treatment_method: Highly beneficial species. Protect and encourage populations in all garden ecosystems.
pest_control.natural_solutions: Provide bug hotels and leaf litter for overwintering adults.
pest_control.prevention: Avoid broad-spectrum chemical insecticides that kill ladybird larvae.

result.interesting_facts: A single Seven-Spot Ladybird adult or larva can consume over 5,000 aphids during its lifetime, making it an organic gardener's best ally.
